meta.source: Reserve Bank of India, DBIE (via the Data Bank)
meta.revisionPolicy: Each year passes through three stages: the budget estimate (February before the year), the revised estimate (February of the year) and the accounts (provisional in May after the year, audited later). The RBI's tables restate a year as it moves from one stage to the next; each stage is kept as its own series.
meta.coverage: The Centre's accounts month by month, April to the month: receipts, spending, interest and the deficits, ₹ crore, and each as a share of the year's budget estimate
meta.note: RBI Bulletin, Union Government Accounts at a Glance (DBIE report 49, two data providers: the old layout to April 2019 and the new from May 2019, the same fourteen items), from the Controller General of Accounts. Figures are cumulative from April and unaudited (the table's note 1). The share of the budget estimate is computed here against the year's budget estimate (from the row most of the year's months print whose own arithmetic holds; the full budget's figure in election years). A month whose own figures do not add up is left empty. 17 months are left empty: they repeat a year earlier, repeat an earlier month, or do not add up (listed on each series). In 148 months, mostly in the old layout, the table counts borrowing inside capital receipts and total receipts (total receipts equal total expenditure); those two items for those months are in a separate bundle (public-finance-centre-monthly-incl-borrowing). 0 duplicate rows with differing figures were found (the later row wins).
